title: Apple Fitness Feels Half-Baked
body:
Apple Fitness looks sleek but lacks real substance. No workout plans, no strength tracking, no smart coaching. If you’re serious about training, you have to use other apps.

The sharing with friends is a nice touch—but why stop there? Add real group challenges, virtual workouts, and more fun ways to stay connected.

Why are we relying on third-party apps when Apple could lead the way? Stop making this just for new users or future devices. Make it great now, for everyone. You have the tech—use it.

- Workouts are generic. No plans, no progression, no personalization. Just a bunch of random videos.
	•	No strength tracking. You can’t log sets, reps, or weights—basic stuff for anyone lifting or training seriously.
	•	Auto-pause doesn’t work right. Stop at a light or adjust your setup, and your stats get messed up. Other apps figured this out years ago.
	•	No real feedback or coaching. The app collects data but does nothing with it. It doesn’t learn or help you improve.
	•	Barely any motivation tools. No challenges, no milestones, no leaderboard—unless your friends are already on it, and even then it’s just step sharing.
	•	Sharing with friends is decent, but boring. Let us actually do workouts together. Build in virtual group workouts, long-distance challenges, even fitness games.
